prerequisites: Knowledge of theory of machines and mechanisms at degree level
Knowledge of algebra and mathematical methods for solving systems of equations
It is advisable to have successfully completed all first-semester subjects

learning_outcomes.text: Students will be able to formulate the mathematical framework for kinematic and dynamic analysis of a mechanism, based on natural coordinates.
Students will acquire the skill to simulate mechanisms using mathematical calculation tools.
Students will be able to use the results of kinematic and dynamic simulation as a starting point in the design of mechanism control systems.
Students will be able to propose the synthesis of mechanisms based on their mathematical formulation.

teaching_methods: Laboratory practices / field / computer room / language classroom
assessment_rules: For the ordinary May and extraordinary June calls, the assessment will be based on a written test (30%), assignments (60%), and an aptitude scale (10%). The written test is an individual exam, while assignments can be individual or group work. The aptitude scale reflects participation and interactions during activities and tutorials. For the extraordinary December-January call and differentiated evaluation, assessment will only be based on the written test and assignments, with the same weights.
